questions.q: Why does this lesson introduce jq after two lessons of using --query and -o tsv / --output text?
options: Because --query starts to get awkward once you need several fields, a filter condition, or a reshaped result, all crammed into one command-line string
Because --query has been removed from both az and aws CLI
Because jq replaces bash entirely
Because JSON output is no longer supported by az or aws
questions.explain: JMESPath inside --query is powerful but becomes unwieldy for complex extraction; jq is a separate tool built specifically for working with JSON.

options: It's a command-line JSON processor that reads JSON from input and lets you filter and reshape it with its own query language
It's a replacement for the az CLI
It converts bash scripts into Python scripts
It only works with AWS CLI output, not az
questions.explain: jq is a standalone tool for querying and transforming JSON, usable with any command that can emit JSON, including both az and aws.

questions.q: In `az vm list --output json | jq -r '.[] | .name'`, what does `.[]` do?
options: Iterates over every element of the top-level JSON array
Deletes every element of the array
Converts the array into a single string
Only selects the first element
questions.explain: .[] steps through each element of the array that az vm list returns, so .name can then be pulled from each one in turn.

questions.q: What does `select(.State.Name == "running")` do in a jq filter?
options: Keeps only the elements where the condition is true, filtering the JSON down to just running instances
Changes every instance's state to "running"
Stops the script if any instance is not running
Is only valid syntax in az CLI, not jq
questions.explain: select() is jq's filter function — it passes through only the elements for which the given condition evaluates to true.

questions.q: What does the -r flag do when running jq?
options: Prints raw output — string values without the surrounding double quotes jq would normally add
Reverses the order of the JSON array
Runs jq in read-only mode
Recursively searches subdirectories for JSON files
questions.explain: -r (raw output) strips the quotes jq normally wraps around string results, which matters for clean output in a script.
